what: rounding the top edges of a hex head on a shaft with a modelled thread (it froze the app)
method: ISO 68-1 basic profile: H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8. External groove (the space between teeth): a trapezoid P/4 wide at the root radius d/2 - 5H/8, widening by 2 tan30 per unit of radius to 7P/8 at d/2. Internal groove: P/8 wide at the major radius d/2, widening to 3P/4 at the minor radius, cut only where there is material (r >= hole radius). Pappus: volume per turn = 2 pi A rc (A the trapezoid area, rc its centroid radius from the axis); a helical sweep of L/P turns removes exactly (L/P) x that, where each end of the thread is a free end or lies inside material. Shaft D5 h=10 plus a hexagonal head of apothem a=2 (area 2 sqrt3 a^2 = 13.8564), h=3. M5 (P=0.8) over 4 mm from the free bottom end (5 turns): 5 x 2.84480. The pick (z=5) is mid-face: the thread starts at the face's only free end. The top end (z=10) is not free: the hex's corners (2.3094 mm out) lie past the M5 root (2.0670 mm), in the groove's way, so the groove never reaches the head (it used to, from the head end, cutting 1.17 mm into it and clipping its corners into the groove's flank); the stop at z=4 is square inside the shaft, removing exactly 4/P turns (the section is symmetric about its centre line). The six top edges rounded R=r=0.3 with the vertical edges left sharp: the section at depth y below the top is a hexagon of apothem a - d(y), d = r - sqrt(r^2 - (r-y)^2); removed = 2 sqrt3 int (2 a d - d^2) dy = 2 sqrt3 [2 a r^2 (1 - pi/4) - r^3 (5/3 - pi/2)] = 0.25866. V = pi 2.5^2 10 + 41.5692 - 5 x 2.84480 - 0.25866 = 223.4361 mm3. Tolerance 0.02%: the groove is SMLib's exact screw sweep (a groove run from the head end instead removes 0.2 mm3 of the head, 0.09%).
